memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "That same day he removed all the male goats that were streaked or spotted, and all the speckled or spotted female goats (all that had white on them) and all the dark-colored lambs, and he placed them in the care of his sons. Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob continued to tend the rest of Laban's flocks." - Gen 30:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
No sooner is the deal struck than Laban tries to tilt it in his own favour. That very day he removes all the already-marked animals — the very kind Jacob was to receive — and hands them to his sons, putting a three-day journey between them so Jacob cannot even get near them. He wants to make sure Jacob starts with nothing. Once again, Laban schemes to cheat the man who has served him so faithfully.

This is a hard experience many of us know: being treated unfairly despite doing right. Jacob had worked honestly and asked for a fair, modest wage, yet Laban immediately moved to undercut him. It can be deeply discouraging to be dealt with dishonestly by those we have served well.

But here is the encouragement waiting in the story. Laban could scheme all he liked, but he could not outmanoeuvre God. As the next verses show, the Lord would prosper Jacob anyway. No human unfairness can block the blessing God intends for His people.

If you are being treated unjustly, take heart. You do not need to fight dishonesty with dishonesty. Keep doing right, entrust your cause to God, and trust Him to be your defender. The Lord vindicates His people (Ps 135:14); no scheme can thwart His purposes.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I being treated unfairly despite doing right?
2. Am I tempted to fight dishonesty with dishonesty?
3. Can I entrust my cause to God as my defender?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I am treated unjustly, help me to keep doing right and to entrust my cause to You. Be my defender, and let no scheme thwart the good You intend. Amen.
